messages.author: 8704d5859c514b2c
messages.subject: Fitting random effect interactions
parts:
Hi all,

Very new to INLA - I'm trying to migrate a model I have working in MCMCglmm to INLA in order to account for an important spatial component in my data.

The model I have in MCMCglmm is specified like this:

model_simple_3 <- MCMCglmm(fixed = cbind(Abundance, Total.tips) ~ 1,
                  random = ~OTU + Family + Family:OTU,
                  family = "multinomial2",
                  data = OTU_matrix_long, nitt = 500000, prior = prior, thin = 40,
                  pr = F)

The idea is that any random effect specified without an interaction, if significant, provides a test for differences in alpha diversity between factor levels, while any random effect that interacts with OTU provides a test for beta diversity or community turnover between factor levels. There's a bunch of different factors I want to play with, but this is a simple example that I'd like to get working first.

I currently have this as my model specification in INLA:

formula2 <- y ~ -1 +
  f(spatial.field, model=spde) +
  f(OTU, model="iid") +
  f(Family, model="iid") +
  f(OTU2, model="iid",
    replicate = Family)

Mod2 <- inla(formula2,
            data = inla.stack.data(Stack, spde = spde),
            family = "binomial",
            control.compute = list(cpo = TRUE),
            control.predictor = list(A = inla.stack.A(Stack),
                                     compute=T),
            Ntrials = Data$Tot_Tips,
            verbose = F)


However, when I try running this model, I get the following error:

Error in Summary.factor(c(NA, NA, NA, NA, NA, NA, NA, NA, NA, NA, NA,  :
  ‘max’ not meaningful for factors

Is it possible to specify such a model in INLA, and if so, how does one do it?

Cheers,
Jim Downie

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Fitting random effect interactions
parts:
Hi Jim,

I assume one or several of OTU, Family, OTU2, and Family are stored as factors?
The NAs are introduced (by design) by inla.stack(), and different
models require different handling of factors with NAs.
In your case, it looks as if you could pre-transform the factors into
factor level indices instead, with as.numeric(), since they are all
just used for indexing into "iid" random effects.

> as.numeric(factor(c("b","c","a","b")))
[1] 2 3 1 2

This will give the same model as when using an actual factor variable
with an "iid" model, but relieves INLA from having to interpret the
factor variables by itself.

Finn
